pages.title: Check what needs attention
pages.description: Read the Needs Attention strip and go straight to the loan behind a card.
pages.intro: **Needs Attention**, at the top of the Portfolio page, lists what is coming up in your loans and which loans look worth refinancing. Check it when you open the app: each card takes you to the loan, or the refinance, behind it.

sections.title: Read the cards
sections.text: Soonest first, the strip lists balloons due in the next 24 months (Maturity), interest-only periods ending in the next 12 months (IO step-up), rate resets in the next 12 months (ARM reset) and loans you marked out of date (Out of date). Green Refi cards come last.

steps.text: On the **Portfolio** tab, look at **Needs Attention**, under the tabs. Each card names the loan, what happens and when.

marks.label: Needs Attention
marks.text: The red number is how many cards there are.

marks.label: ARM reset (amber)
marks.text: A rate resets soon: the new rate and the date.

marks.label: Maturity (red)
marks.text: A loan comes due: the balloon to pay off and the date.

steps.text: Scroll the strip sideways to see the other cards. The green **Refi** cards at the end are loans priced more than 0.25% above what the same loan would cost today, the biggest gap first.

marks.label: Refi (green)
marks.text: Priced above today’s market, and by how much.

marks.label: Another Refi card
marks.text: Sorted by how far above market, the biggest gap first.

callouts.text: A card with a pink outline is three months away or less.

sections.title: Open the loan behind a card

steps.text: Click a **Maturity**, **IO step-up** or **ARM reset** card. The loan opens, and its payment schedule scrolls to the month of the event, lit up for a few seconds.

marks.label: That month
marks.text: The payment where the event happens; here the final payment, with the balloon.

marks.label: Pays on
marks.text: The day the payment is due: the date on the card.

steps.text: Scroll up and click **Whole Portfolio** to go back.

sections.title: Open the refinance behind a Refi card

steps.text: Click a **Refi** card. The refinance for that loan opens.

marks.label: Refinance Analysis
marks.text: The refinance for the loan on the card.

marks.label: No T12 yet
marks.text: This sample property has no T12, so nothing is sized yet. Its button opens Underwriting for it.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Back to where you were.

steps.text: Click **Close** to go back.

callouts.text: A refinance is sized on the property’s T12 and the underwriting approved from it, never on a typed NOI. See [Upload a T12](upload-a-t12).

next.text: Every maturity and reset, month by month.
Every part of the Portfolio page, named.

pages.title: Check each property’s coverage
pages.description: See which properties clear your DSCR, debt-yield and LTV targets, and add the NOI of the ones without one.
pages.intro: The Portfolio page measures the whole book, and every property in it, against your targets: a minimum DSCR, a minimum debt yield and a maximum LTV. Check it to find the properties that miss a target, the ones with no NOI yet, and the ones paying well above today’s market rate.

callouts.text: The targets (1.25×, 8% …) are set in Settings. See [Set the portfolio targets](set-portfolio-targets).

steps.text: On the **Portfolio** tab, read **Portfolio DSCR** and **Portfolio Debt Yield**, under the heading. Each says how the whole book stands against your target.

marks.label: Portfolio DSCR
marks.text: Total NOI ÷ total yearly loan payments, against your minimum DSCR.

marks.label: Portfolio Debt Yield
marks.text: Total NOI ÷ total balance, against your minimum debt yield.

steps.text: Look at **Coverage vs targets**, under the tiles. Each bar is the portfolio’s figure and the thin dark line is your target: green clears it, amber is close, red is off. Under the bars, every property that is off a target is named.

marks.label: Portfolio DSCR
marks.text: Against your minimum DSCR.

marks.label: Portfolio LTV
marks.text: Against your maximum LTV: lower is better here.

marks.label: Off a target
marks.text: Every property that misses a target or has no NOI yet.

callouts.text: A property with no NOI yet counts as $0 NOI, so its debt pulls the portfolio’s DSCR and debt yield down. The tiles say how many such properties there are.

steps.text: Scroll down to **Coverage**. Each row is one property, worst DSCR first; a senior loan and its mezzanine count as one. Properties with no NOI yet are at the bottom.

marks.label: DSCR
marks.text: NOI ÷ yearly loan payments. Green clears the target, amber is close, red is off.

marks.label: Gap
marks.text: The property’s rate today minus the market’s. Green: more than 0.25% above market.

marks.label: Off target
marks.text: Misses at least one target.

marks.label: Needs T12/NOI
marks.text: No NOI yet.

steps.text: Read the tag at the end of each row: **clears** meets all three targets, **off target** misses at least one, and **needs T12/NOI** has no NOI yet.
Compare **Current** with **Market**: the rate the property pays now against what the same loan would cost today. A green **Gap** is worth a look at a refinance.

callouts.text: The picture shows the first rows; the table lists every property.

steps.text: Click **Add NOI** on a property marked needs T12/NOI.

Type the property’s yearly NOI in **Property annual NOI**, from its operating statement. Change **Cap rate** only if you have a better figure than the default for its type; it gives the value, and so the LTV.

marks.label: Property annual NOI
marks.text: The yearly NOI, in dollars. It must be more than $0.

marks.label: Cap rate
marks.text: Filled in by property type. Value = NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Continue
marks.text: Saves the NOI and the cap rate.

steps.text: Click **Continue**. The row shows its DSCR, debt yield and LTV, and every total on the page counts it.

callouts.text: The property’s T12 gives a better NOI, and it is the only one a refinance uses. See [Upload a T12](upload-a-t12). (The NOI in the picture is made up and was not saved.)

steps.text: Click **Refi path** on the property’s row. The refinance opens for that property, all its loans together.

marks.label: Refinance Analysis
marks.text: The refinance for that property. Without a T12 it says “No T12 yet”.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Back to the Portfolio page.

steps.text: Click **Close** to come back.

callouts.text: To put several properties under one new loan, click **Create a portfolio…** above the Coverage table. See [Refinance several loans together](refinance-together).

next.text: Give a property its NOI from its T12.
Every column of the Coverage table.

pages.title: See the forecast and a rate shock
pages.description: See what the book will cost to carry in the years ahead, and what a move in rates would do.
pages.intro: The **Debt-Service Forecast** shows each year’s debt service ahead, with the balloons coming due if you want them. **Rate Shock**, under it, shows what rates 1% lower, or 1% or 2% higher, would do to your payments.

steps.text: On the **Portfolio** tab, scroll down to **Debt-Service Forecast**. Each bar is a year’s debt service (principal and interest plus escrows and fees), from this year on. Point at a bar to see its amount.

marks.label: This year
marks.text: Darker, with its label in bold.

marks.label: 1yr
marks.text: One bar per year (shown).

marks.label: Recurring
marks.text: Regular payments only (shown).

steps.text: Click **3yr** or **5yr** to group the years into longer bars. **1yr** goes back.
Click **+ Payoffs** to stack the balloons coming due on top of each bar. **Recurring** shows only the regular payments again.

marks.label: 3yr
marks.text: On: three-year bars.

marks.label: + Payoffs
marks.text: On: balloons stacked on top.

marks.label: A three-year bar
marks.text: Green: debt service. Dark: balloons due.

marks.label: Key
marks.text: Which color is which.

sections.title: Check a rate shock
sections.text: Fixed loans don’t move. Floating loans move at once. Hybrid ARMs move only when they reset.

steps.text: Scroll down to **Rate Shock**. The bar at the top splits the book into fixed, ARM and floating.
Read the table: for rates 1% lower (−100 bps), today’s, and 1% or 2% higher, the blended rate, the monthly debt service, and the interest per year more (red) or less (green) than today.

marks.label: Fixed / ARM / Floating
marks.text: Green fixed, amber ARM, red floating.

marks.label: Scenarios
marks.text: −100 bps, Today, +100 bps, +200 bps (100 bps = 1%).

marks.label: In plain words
marks.text: What each +1% costs per year, and its share of your yearly debt service.

marks.label: Most exposed
marks.text: The largest floating and ARM loans.

next.text: When each balloon and reset falls.
Every part of the forecast and Rate Shock.

pages.title: Find a loan in the portfolio
pages.description: Find a loan in Portfolio detail, by property or by lender, and open it.
pages.intro: **Portfolio detail**, near the bottom of the Portfolio page, lists every loan grouped by property, largest balance first. Find the loan there and click it to open its page.

steps.text: On the **Portfolio** tab, scroll down to **Portfolio detail**. A property with one loan is one row.

marks.label: A one-loan property
marks.text: Click to open its loan.

marks.label: A property with 2 loans
marks.text: One bold row with the number of loans.

steps.text: For a property with a senior and a mezzanine loan, click its bold row. Its loans show under it, marked Senior or Mezz. Click the row again to hide them.

marks.label: Open property
marks.text: Click again to hide its loans.

marks.label: Senior loan
marks.text: The first-lien loan.

marks.label: Mezz loan
marks.text: The mezzanine loan behind it.

steps.text: Click the loan. Its page opens on the **Specific Property** side.

marks.label: Specific Property
marks.text: Now showing one property.

marks.label: The property
marks.text: The one you clicked; pick another here.

marks.label: Whole Portfolio
marks.text: Back to the Portfolio page.

steps.text: Click **Whole Portfolio** to come back.
Click **All lenders**, above the table. Every lender is listed with what is owed to it.
Tick one or more lenders. The table keeps only their properties; a property with two loans opens to show the matching one.

marks.label: Ticked
marks.text: Only this lender’s loans are shown.

marks.label: 1 lender
marks.text: How many lenders are picked.

marks.label: Share
marks.text: Their share of the whole book.

marks.label: Clear
marks.text: Shows every lender again.

steps.text: Click **Clear** to show every lender again.

next.text: Open a loan from the property list instead.
Every part of a loan’s page.

pages.title: The Portfolio page
pages.description: Every part of the Portfolio page, from Needs Attention at the top to the removed and archived items at the bottom.
pages.intro: The **Portfolio** tab with **Whole Portfolio** picked: the whole book on one page. Every active loan counts in it; removed, paid-off and archived ones don’t. Each picture names its controls.

sections.title: Needs Attention
sections.text: Soonest first: balloons due in the next 24 months, interest-only periods ending in the next 12 months, rate resets in the next 12 months and loans flagged out of date; then the Refi cards. A card with a pink outline is three months away or less. Scroll the strip sideways to see every card. See [Check what needs attention](check-what-needs-attention).

views.title: The date cards
views.text: Click one: the loan opens, with its schedule at the month of the event.

marks.label: Needs Attention
marks.text: The strip’s title; the red number is how many cards there are.

marks.label: ARM reset (amber)
marks.text: An adjustable rate resets soon: the new rate and the date.

marks.label: Maturity (red)
marks.text: A loan comes due: the balloon to pay off and the date.

views.title: Further along the strip
views.text: Scroll sideways for the rest of the date cards.

marks.label: IO step-up (orange)
marks.text: An interest-only period ends: the new monthly payment and the date it starts.

views.title: The Refi cards
views.text: At the end of the strip: loans whose rate is more than 0.25% above what the same loan would cost today. Click one to open its refinance.

marks.label: Refi (green)
marks.text: Priced above today’s market, and by how much.

marks.label: Another Refi card
marks.text: Sorted by how far above market, the biggest gap first.

views.text: Four figures to read, not buttons. Portfolio DSCR = the total NOI of every property ÷ the total yearly principal-and-interest payments of every loan (during an interest-only period, the full amortizing payment is used). A property with no NOI yet counts as $0 NOI, and the tile says how many there are.

marks.label: Loan count
marks.text: How many active loans the page covers.

marks.label: Priced above market
marks.text: How many properties pay more than 0.25% above today’s market rate (the Refi cards).

marks.label: Total Debt Outstanding
marks.text: What is owed today on every loan; under it, the number of loans and what they were when first made.

marks.label: Weighted-Avg Rate
marks.text: The average interest rate, weighted by balance; under it, the total monthly debt service (payments plus escrows and fees).

marks.label: Portfolio DSCR
marks.text: Total NOI ÷ total yearly loan payments, against your minimum DSCR target.

marks.label: Portfolio Debt Yield
marks.text: Total NOI ÷ total balance, against your minimum debt-yield target.

views.text: What kind of debt you have, when it comes due, and how the book stands against its targets. Point at a bar in “Debt maturing by year” to see its amount.

marks.label: Debt by rate type
marks.text: Today’s balance split into fixed, hybrid ARM and floating; the total in the middle.

marks.label: Legend
marks.text: Each type’s color and its balance.

marks.label: A year’s maturities
marks.text: What comes due that year. Amber = in the next two years, green = later.

marks.label: Portfolio DSCR
marks.text: The bar is the portfolio’s figure, the thin dark line your minimum DSCR. Green clears it, amber is close, red is off.

marks.label: Portfolio LTV
marks.text: Balance ÷ value (value = NOI ÷ cap rate), against your maximum LTV: lower is better here.

marks.label: Portfolio Debt Yield
marks.text: Against your minimum debt yield.

marks.label: Off a target
marks.text: Every property that misses a target; “no NOI” means its T12 or NOI isn’t in yet.

views.title: The Coverage table
views.text: One row per property (a senior loan and its mezzanine count as one), worst DSCR first; properties with no NOI yet at the bottom. The picture shows the first rows.

marks.label: Coverage
marks.text: DSCR, debt yield and LTV per property, against your targets.

marks.label: Create a portfolio…
marks.text: Puts several properties under one new loan (below).

marks.label: NOI
marks.text: The property’s yearly net operating income.

marks.label: DSCR
marks.text: NOI ÷ yearly loan payments. Green clears the target, amber is close, red is off.

marks.label: Debt Yield
marks.text: NOI ÷ balance.

marks.label: LTV
marks.text: Balance ÷ value (value = NOI ÷ cap rate).

marks.label: Current
marks.text: The rate the property pays now (blended across its loans).

marks.label: Market
marks.text: What the same loan would cost today, from today’s rates.

marks.label: Gap
marks.text: Current minus Market. Green (more than 0.25%): worth looking at a refinance.

marks.label: Clears
marks.text: Meets all three targets.

marks.label: Off target
marks.text: Misses at least one target.

marks.label: Needs T12/NOI
marks.text: No NOI yet: add the T12 in Underwriting, or type the NOI (Add NOI).

marks.label: Refi path
marks.text: Opens the refinance for this property, all its loans together.

marks.label: Add NOI
marks.text: Type the property’s NOI (below).

views.title: Add NOI
views.text: For a property with no NOI yet. The figure in the picture is made up and was not saved.

marks.label: Annual NOI
marks.text: This window asks for one property’s NOI.

marks.label: Property annual NOI
marks.text: The yearly NOI in dollars, from the property’s operating statement. It must be more than $0.

marks.label: Cap rate
marks.text: Used to estimate the value (NOI ÷ cap rate), and so the LTV. Filled in by property type; change it if you have a better figure.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes without saving.

marks.label: Continue
marks.text: Saves the NOI and cap rate; the table and the totals update.

views.title: Create a portfolio…
views.text: Puts several properties under one new loan. **Create the portfolio** opens the refinance of them together; nothing changes until you save the new loan there. See [Refinance several loans together](refinance-together).

marks.label: Create a portfolio
marks.text: One new loan on several properties.

marks.label: Find a property
marks.text: Type part of a name to shorten the list.

marks.label: Tick
marks.text: Tick each property the new loan will cover.

marks.label: Owes / NOI
marks.text: What is owed on the property today (or “no loan yet”), and the NOI the refinance would use: its T12’s or its approved underwriting’s, or “no T12”.

marks.label: Totals
marks.text: How many are ticked, the loans that would be paid off and what they owe, and the NOI together; or which ones have no T12 yet.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes the list.

marks.label: Create the portfolio
marks.text: Opens the refinance of the ticked properties.

views.text: Each bar is a year’s debt service (principal and interest plus escrows and fees), from this year on. Point at a bar to see its amount. See [See the forecast and a rate shock](see-the-forecast).

marks.label: Debt-Service Forecast
marks.text: Yearly debt service ahead.

marks.label: 1yr
marks.text: One bar per year (shown).

marks.label: 3yr
marks.text: One bar per three years.

marks.label: 5yr
marks.text: One bar per five years.

marks.label: Recurring
marks.text: Regular payments only (shown).

marks.label: + Payoffs
marks.text: Stacks the balloons due on top of each bar, with a key under the chart.

marks.label: This year
marks.text: This year’s debt service: darker, with its label in bold.

views.text: What happens to your payments if rates move. Fixed loans don’t move; floating loans move at once; hybrid ARMs move only when they reset.

marks.label: Rate Shock
marks.text: How much of the book is floating or ARM, and what share that is.

marks.label: Fixed / ARM / Floating
marks.text: The book split by rate type: green fixed, amber ARM, red floating.

marks.label: Scenarios
marks.text: −100 bps, Today, +100 bps, +200 bps (100 bps = 1%): blended rate, monthly debt service, and interest per year more (red) or less (green) than today.

marks.label: In plain words
marks.text: What each +1% costs per year, and its share of your yearly debt service.

marks.label: Now or at reset
marks.text: How much moves at once (floating) and how much only when the ARMs reset.

marks.label: Most exposed
marks.text: The largest floating and ARM loans.

sections.title: Portfolio detail
sections.text: Every loan, grouped by property, largest balance first. See [Find a loan in the portfolio](find-a-loan).

views.title: The Properties table
views.text: A property with one loan is one row; click it to open the loan. A property with a senior and a mezzanine loan is one bold row: click it to show its loans. Properties with no loan yet are at the bottom. The picture shows the first rows.

marks.label: Portfolio detail
marks.text: Every loan, grouped by property.

marks.label: Properties
marks.text: The table.

marks.label: Top lender
marks.text: Which lender holds the most of your debt, and its share.

marks.label: All lenders
marks.text: Filters the table by lender (below).

marks.label: A property with 2 loans
marks.text: Click to show (or hide) its loans. Its row shows the combined balance, blended rate and total monthly P&I.

marks.label: A one-loan property
marks.text: Click to open its loan.

marks.label: Status
marks.text: The loan’s status (Active, or a flag such as Out of date).

views.title: Filter by lender
views.text: Tick one or more lenders and the table keeps only their properties.

marks.label: Filter by lender
marks.text: Every lender in the book.

marks.label: Ticked
marks.text: Only this lender’s loans are shown.

marks.label: Balance
marks.text: What is owed to that lender.

marks.label: Clear
marks.text: Shows every lender again.

marks.label: 1 lender
marks.text: How many lenders are picked.

marks.label: Share
marks.text: Their share of the whole book.

sections.title: Removed, paid-off and archived
sections.text: At the bottom of the page: what was taken out of the totals. See [Bring back a removed loan or property](bring-back-removed). Here a sample loan was removed and a sample property archived.

views.text: A loan you remove (in its Loan Record) or mark as paid off is listed in the grey strip. A property you archive (**Remove** under Specific Property) leaves the lists, the totals and the count with all its loans, and is listed in the amber strip; its files stay.

marks.label: Removed & paid-off loans
marks.text: How many loans are out of the totals.

marks.label: The loan
marks.text: Its name, its status (Removed or Paid off) and the date.

marks.label: Restore
marks.text: Puts it back in every total, tile and the calendar.

marks.label: Delete permanently
marks.text: The bin: deletes the loan record (it asks first).

marks.label: Archived
marks.text: How many properties are archived.

marks.label: Un-archive
marks.text: Click the name: the property and its loans come back to the lists, the totals and the count.

marks.label: Delete permanently
marks.text: The bin: deletes the property and its files (it asks first).

sections.title: Adding a property
sections.text: **Add Property** is on the **Specific Property** side of the switch under the tabs. A new property joins this page at once. See [Add a property](add-a-property).

views.title: The Add Property window
views.text: A name is enough: its loans, T12, rent roll and documents can come later.

marks.label: Add a property
marks.text: Adds a property to the portfolio.

marks.label: Property name
marks.text: The name only (a made-up one here). Empty, the window asks for one.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes without adding anything.

marks.label: Create
marks.text: Adds the property.

views.title: A new property on this page
views.text: It sits at the bottom of the Properties table, marked No loan yet. It also counts in the property count, and in coverage once it has an NOI.

marks.label: The new property
marks.text: Click to open it in Underwriting, where its T12 goes and its loan can be added.

marks.label: No loan yet
marks.text: It has no loan yet.

views.title: A name like one you have
views.text: A name like a property you already have asks first. (The exact name of a property you have isn’t added twice; the name of one of your loans offers to add a loan to that property instead.)

marks.label: Similar to …
marks.text: The property it looks like.

marks.label: Which one
marks.text: The name you typed and the one you already have.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing is added.

marks.label: Create anyway
marks.text: Adds the new property: they are different buildings.

marks.label: Open it
marks.text: Opens the property you already have.

pages.title: Bring back a removed loan or property
pages.description: Restore a removed or paid-off loan, or un-archive a property, from the bottom of the Portfolio page.
pages.intro: A loan you remove or mark as paid off, and a property you archive, leave every total but are kept. The bottom of the Portfolio page lists them: bring one back exactly as it was, or delete it for good.

steps.text: On the **Portfolio** tab, scroll to the bottom. Removed and paid-off loans are in the grey strip; archived properties are in the amber strip.

marks.label: A removed loan
marks.text: Its name, Removed or Paid off, and the date.

marks.label: Restore
marks.text: Brings the loan back.

marks.label: An archived property
marks.text: Click its name to bring it back.

steps.text: For a loan, click **Restore**. It goes back into every total, tile and the calendar, exactly as it was.
For a property, click its name in the **Archived** strip. The property and its loans come back to the lists, the totals and the property count, with its files.
Click the bin next to the loan. It asks first.

marks.label: Delete permanently?
marks.text: The loan it is about.

marks.label: What happens
marks.text: Gone for good; the automatic backups keep a copy. The property stays, with its files.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Keeps the loan in the list.

marks.label: Delete permanently
marks.text: Deletes the record.

steps.text: For an archived property, click the bin next to its name. The window lists what will be deleted with it.

marks.label: Delete permanently?
marks.text: Here, an archived property.

marks.label: What is deleted
marks.text: The property with its loans and its files. Portfolio chats that mention it are kept.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Keeps it archived.

marks.label: Delete permanently
marks.text: Deletes it for good.

steps.text: Click **Delete permanently**, or **Cancel** to keep it.

callouts.text: Delete permanently can’t be undone in the app. Only a backup brings it back: the automatic backups keep a copy. See [Back up and restore](back-up-and-restore).

next.text: Remove a loan from its Loan Record.
Bring back something deleted, from a backup.
